passage: Saturday in the park: Sangeeta blew bubbles and Gopika squealed, chasing them. When the bottle ran dry she flopped down and wailed. Sunday at Nani's: Gopika grabbed a warm jalebi, sticky and sweet, and cried when Nani moved the plate away. Monday night: Gopika snuggled into Sangeeta's lap for a cuddle. When Sangeeta stood up, she howled with her arms up. Sangeeta sat back down and sang softly. Gopika sighed and melted against her.

qa.q: What did Gopika grab at Nani's?
qa.a: A warm jalebi, sticky and sweet.

qa.q: Why did Gopika howl on Monday night?
qa.a: She wanted the warm cuddle to go on, and she was upset when Sangeeta stood up and it stopped.

qa.q: What choice on Monday night helped Gopika settle?
qa.a: Sangeeta sat back down and sang softly, giving a little more comfort so Gopika could calm down.

qa.q: What is it like for Sangeeta when every nice thing ends in tears?
qa.a: Sangeeta may feel tired by the crying, but she seems to understand that Gopika is simply chasing sweet, cosy things, and responds gently.

grounding: Over three days a toddler seeks bubbles, sweets and cuddles and cries each time they stop.

qa.a: On the ninth-floor balcony.

qa.a: She might feel a little torn between cooking and his tears, but she knows he is just a toddler loving the fun, so she comforts him.

grounding: A toddler delights in bubbles and cries when they stop, calming with a cuddle and something soft to eat.

passage:
Daycare note, Monday. Afreen, Toddler Room.
Zubin (2) wanted to stay on my lap all morning, patting my cheek and saying "more hug." When I put him down to help another child, he cried loudly. At lunch he loved the sweet rice and wailed when the bowl was empty.
I gave him one more cuddle and his soft blanket, then showed him the water tray. He splashed and giggled within minutes.
Next: tell his father at pickup. Wanting sweets and cuddles is normal at his age. 🙂

qa.q: What did Zubin say while patting Afreen's cheek?
qa.a: More hug.

qa.q: Why did Zubin wail when his bowl was empty?
qa.a: He loved the sweet rice and wanted more of that good feeling right away, so its ending upset him.

qa.q: What did Afreen do that helped Zubin, and why did it work?
qa.a: Afreen gave him one more cuddle and his soft blanket, then moved him to the water tray, which comforted him and gave him a new pleasure.

qa.q: How might Zubin's father feel reading this note?
qa.a: He would probably feel reassured that Zubin's crying for cuddles and sweets is normal and that he was comforted.

grounding: It shows a toddler who seeks cuddles and sweet food and cries when they stop, a natural wish for comfort and pleasure at this age.

passage:
At the jaggery crusher at the edge of the village, steam rose from the big pan. Irfan Chacha scraped a warm, soft piece of jaggery and gave it to Abhinav, two, who sat on his Dadi's hip.
Abhinav sucked it, eyes closing, sticky to the elbows. When it was gone he held out his hand. "More!" Dadi said no. His face crumpled, and he wailed.
Dadi pressed him to her warm shawl and swayed. Abhinav sniffed, then fell asleep on her shoulder.

qa.q: Who gave Abhinav the jaggery?
qa.a: Irfan Chacha.

qa.q: Why did Abhinav wail when the jaggery was gone?
qa.a: He was enjoying the warm, sweet jaggery so much that he wanted more at once, and losing it upset him.

qa.q: What did Dadi do that helped, and why did it work?
qa.a: She held him close in her warm shawl and swayed, giving him a different comfort, a cuddle, so he could settle and sleep.

qa.q: How might Irfan Chacha see Abhinav's crying?
qa.a: He would likely see it as a toddler simply loving something sweet, and might smile at how quickly the cuddle calmed him.

grounding: It shows a toddler seeking warm, sweet jaggery and a cuddle and crying when the sweet stops, a simple drive for pleasure and comfort at this age.
